summary: A white tower on Cape Capstan at the mouth of the Apple River, on Chignecto Bay: the third light on the point, after the first burned in 1869.

lens.note: Dioptric apparatus: seventh order by 1902 (Department report); 5th-order dioptric with steam fog signal 1922-1941 (NSLPS). The current lens is not stated.

structures.type: square concrete tower with lantern and gallery, on a fog-signal building until the building was removed
structures.note: Build year conflicts: 1965 (record, Wikidata), c.1965 and 1966-70 (NSLPS), 1968 (Lighthouse Friends), 1972 (Lighthouse Directory).

structures.type: square wooden tower, lantern on the roof of a dwelling
structures.note: Built by John Livingstone for $1,180; replaced the 1848 tower (Lighthouse Friends; NSLPS).

structures.type: square white tower on the roof of a dwelling

access.note: Coast Guard property. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Visible across the bay from Apple River Road; a logging road down the peninsula ends long before the light (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: First light on Hetty Point, Cape Capstan; NSLPS 'Began: 1848'. Lighthouse Friends: a decade after the 1838 proposal.
Light shown from two windows at the west end, with catoptric lenses (NSLPS)
Tower and dwelling burned on 9 August 1869, while keeper James Tate was away (Lighthouse Friends)
Replacement tower 100 ft SSE of the old one, in operation 1 October 1870, built by John Livingstone for $1,180 (Lighthouse Friends; NSLPS)
NSLPS: fog signal established 1889. Lighthouse Friends gives 1899 for a fog alarm moved here from St. Martin's Head.
Fog alarm moved from St. Martin's Head, New Brunswick; George A. Briggs transferred to look after it (Lighthouse Friends)
Catoptric apparatus changed to dioptric of the seventh order (Department report, year ended 1902)
Repairs to the fog alarm, $176.64 (Department's repairs list)
5th-order dioptric lens with steam fog signal, dated 1922-1941 (NSLPS)
New type B diaphone with two 6-hp gasoline engines and two 8x6 compressors (Department report, fiscal 1922-23)
Type B diaphone with three pistons installed in place of the old diaphone (Department report, fiscal 1923-24)
Present tower built at the corner of a one-storey fog-signal building (Lighthouse Friends). Other dates: c.1965 and 1966-70 (NSLPS); 1972 (Lighthouse Directory).
Keepers' two dwellings removed from the site (Lighthouse Friends)
Fog signal discontinued by 1992 (NSLPS); the one-storey fog building was later torn down and the tower's lantern room removed (Lighthouse Friends)
Coast Guard refurbished the tower and installed a new lantern room (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Directory)

corrections.why: NSLPS gives 'Began: 1848' for the first light on Hetty Point, and Lighthouse Friends' 1838-to-1848 account fits. 1870 is when the second tower went into operation (Lighthouse Friends; NSLPS).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1902 report says the apparatus became dioptric of the seventh order; the Preservation Society dates a 5th-order dioptric lens to 1922-1941. Both can be true with a change between them; the sources do not say which lens was in place from 1902 to 1922.

Lighthouse Friends gives forty feet (12 m) above the water for the 1848 light; the Preservation Society gives 64 feet (19.5 m) for Apple River I. The story states both; the sources do not reconcile them.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster is Lighthouse Friends' list (facts only); its keeper dates for Elliott (to 1965) and McNally (from 1960) overlap. Elderkin's 1905 start is from the Department's 1909 keepers' appointments (scan 166, printed 159); the OCR reads the day and month as 'tt 31, 1905'. The Apple River pairing is from the Department's 1910 table (scan 256, printed 254), where 'Apple River Light and Fog Alarm' and 'Hill E. Elderkin' sit on one OCR line. The 1905 and 1906 keepers' lists were dropped because their names and stations sit in separate OCR blocks. The page images for scan 166 and scan 256 were NOT viewed: the built-in browser refused archive.org, so the checker must read them before this goes out. Briggs's dates conflict within Lighthouse Friends and are left without years. Present-tower dates conflict (1965 record, c.1965, 1966-70, 1968, 1972); the record's 1965 is Wikidata's. Fog-signal date conflicts: NSLPS 1889 and Lighthouse Friends 1899 (a moved alarm); unresolved. First-light height: Lighthouse Friends 40 ft, NSLPS 64 ft; both are stated in the story. The fiscal 1922-23 and 1923-24 Department reports both record a type B diaphone at Apple River (the first new, with two engines and compressors; the second with three pistons, replacing the old diaphone); the sources do not say whether these are two installations or one reported twice, and the story gives both as recorded. Record correction: first_lit 1870 should be 1848 (the first light). Record boat_only: true is not supported by these sources; Lighthouse Friends describes road access to the light's view and says the logging road ends well short, so the access wording was left unresolved. Tate's 1869 account is printed by Lighthouse Friends; the original is not in the corpus and is cited second-hand. Lighthouse Friends' 1838 Commissioners quotation is second-hand and paraphrased.
